text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.9% today to close at $421.85, continuing a strong two-week rally that has gained 9% overall. The main driver appears to be relief in crude oil markets: while US oil prices remain elevated at $107 per barrel, Saudi Arabia signaled it would increase crude exports following a pipeline attack, easing supply concerns that had driven prices higher. At the same time, refineries are running at 96.8% capacity—near maximum utilization—which means MPC benefits from both tighter crude supplies (supporting margins) and strong demand for refined products like diesel, which has hit record prices and is squeezing the broader economy.

The bigger picture is that geopolitical risk around Iran and the Middle East appears to be receding. Trump's comments about winding down Iran tensions, combined with Saudi Arabia's willingness to release more oil, have reduced the threat of severe supply disruptions that would have benefited refiners in the short term but signaled economic stress. Paradoxically, refiners like MPC thrive when they can run full capacity with healthy margins—which is where the market sits now—rather than when energy chaos creates temporary windfalls.
